column1: # Setting patches (dm/games/README.md, Setting patches): words of the game's code the host writes at launch when a setting has a value, each after checking the original word on the build it was found in.
# Shadows (static analysis of main e25c90c1… / v458752, checked against the rewriter's main.changed.tsv: no word is one the rewriter changed; README.md, Shadow settings)
# Shadow resolution: the per-frame shadow size (main+0x8186c) scales the preset size by max(renderW / 1920, renderH / 1080); fcsel s0,s0,s1,gt -> fmov s0,#1.0 keeps the full preset size
# Shadow map size: the quality presets built at stage start (main+0x6edda4) all ask for 2048: mov w26,#0x800 (Console, Handheld) and movk x26,#0x800,lsl #32 (UltraQuality, HighQuality)
# Upscale ratio, dynamic resolution and effects resolution (static analysis of main e25c90c1… / v458752; README.md, Resolution model). The scene renders at the upscaler's
# output / the current rate (main+0x38db98, the dynamic-resolution controller): it walks a table of rates (count <= 9) between 1.0 (no upscaler) and NdsrUpscaleMaxRate,
# stepping toward sharper only while the rate is above NdsrUpscaleMinRate (SystemData/ProjectGraphicsParam Default: 1.375 and 2.0, which replace the code defaults 1.375 and 1.9),
# and stores it into the rate state (+0xc of [[ctrl+0xf0]+0x270]; the only other writer is the param apply at main+0x1605320, which snaps the same way)
# Upscaler quality (a fixed rate R, DM_UPSCALE_DYNAMIC unset or 0): every frame takes the controller's fixed-rate path (tbz w8,#1 -> b main+0x38de6c), whose rate is fmov s8,#R,
# and the store takes R itself (ldr s0,[x9] -> fmov s0,#R at main+0x38df08, past the table snap), as does the param apply (main+0x16053a4). R <= 1.0 turns the upscaler off
# (the controller's own flag and mip bias, as at its own 1.0). Only fmov immediates: Balanced is 1.6875 (27/16), not 1.7
# Dynamic resolution (DM_UPSCALE_DYNAMIC=1, rates up to 1.6875): the controller runs as shipped with NdsrUpscaleMinRate R and NdsrUpscaleMaxRate 2.0 (its four reads at
# main+0x38dd04 / 0x38dd98 / 0x38e104 / 0x38e194 become fmov), so it steps among its table's rates between R and 2.0. Ultra performance (3.0, a rate the game never
# chooses) only with DM_UPSCALER metalfx or metalfx-temporal: agl's network was never run that far

column1: # HDR highlights (DM_HDR=1, the HDR setting; no row of its own; README.md, HDR highlights): agl's alHdrCompose takes each channel through a normalised logistic of steepness K before its
# shoulder (n(c) = (s(K(c-w)) - s(-Kw)) / (s(K(1-w)) - s(-Kw)), w = DRSigmoidMid 0.5, L = 1 - exp(-luma(n)), shoulder knee 0.65, exponent 0.75, top M = peak / paper white).
# main+0x1b9af0 ldr s1,[x11,#0x18] loads K (DRSigmoidGain, the stage environment's env+0x708: the class default 1.0 in every Env archive of v458752, written by nothing at run time),
# which caps the brightest pixel at 1.33 x paper white whatever the peak. fmov s1,#K sets it: for each band of hdr_peak (the reported peak / paper white), the largest K fmov encodes
# whose modelled ceiling is at least 98 % of the peak (edges from the captured frame's fit, w 0.484, rounded down: up to 0.06 below w 0.5's, and at least 98 % for both)

column1: # Frame rate (README.md, Frame rate lock): the frame-rate controller main+0x204a18 (called once a frame from main+0x203718 while VRR is off) turns the frame's measure (frame start to the
# later of its submission and the GPU's end, in vsyncs v) into a target interval trunc(v + margin -0.2) + 1 at main+0x204ab0 (fcvtzs w9,s0; main+0x204ab4 add w10,w9,#1), clamps it to the
# controller's [min, max] (main+0x204ab8-0x204ac4), steps up after 2 frames above the current interval and down, one step at a time, after 6 frames below it unless a registered listener sets
# its veto byte (main+0x204b8c ldrb w8,[sp,#0x18]; main+0x204b90 cbnz w8 -> keep). mov w9,#(N-1) makes the target N before the same clamp, so the game's own present-interval path, its min / max
# (cutscenes) and the frozen-interval path (main+0x204a4c) are untouched. Locked 60 also skips the veto (cbnz -> nop; the listeners are still called), so a step down to 60 is never refused
